title: Access NYC311 as a Person with a Disability
body:
Our website supports screen readers. If you experience any issues, you can leave us [feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02419) - it helps us improve!
If you prefer assistance, an NYC311 representative can help by phone or text. You can dial 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) or text us at [311-692](sms:311692).

title: Access NYC311 as a Person with a Disability
body:
You can text us directly to reach a live NYC311 representative at [311-692](sms:311692). The NYC311 Text Team is trained to provide information and handle most NYC311 reports based on complexity. If you’re being asked to call 311 but are unable to, let the representative know. We’ll do our best to assist you by text.
If you use 711, video relay services, or another relay provider, your relay operator can connect you with 311 by dialing 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675).

title: Access NYC311 as a Person with a Disability
body:

If you use 711, video relay services, or another relay provider, your relay operator can connect you with 311 by dialing 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675).

title: Access NYC311 as a Person with a Disability
body:
For those who prefer to use NYC311 online or the [NYC311 App](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01025), our content is intentionally written to be easy to understand. If there’s an area you think we could improve, let us know by providing [feedback](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02419).
If self-service is challenging, a live NYC311 representative is here to assist with guided support 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
Just text [311-692](sms:311692) and a representative will reply shortly. Our representatives are trained to communicate clearly, repeat information, and guide you at your pace.
Or call [311](tel:311) or 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) to connect with us.

body:
NYC311 doesn’t have an in-person location, but we can be reached by:

We are here for you 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year!
If you have limited hand mobility, a voice assistant like Siri may help you place a call. When using a voice assistant to contact us, please be sure to say or enter our full number: 212-NEW-YORK [(212-639-9675)](tel:2126399675) .

title: Mandatory Downspout Disconnection
body:
New York City property owners must ensure their downspouts (rain gutters) are not connected to the City’s sanitary sewer system. These connections are not allowed under [New York City’s Rules](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/newyorkcity/latest/NYCrules/0-0-0-26985) because they can overwhelm the sewer with rainwater and cause sewer back-ups in basements and flooding in neighborhoods. The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) plans to start enforcing this rule.
If your downspouts are currently connected to the City’s sanitary sewer system, you must disconnect them. You can disconnect them yourself, or you can hire a contractor.
[Get more information and guidance for DEP's Mandatory Downspout Disconnection.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/whats-new/downspout-disconnection.page)
Tips For Redirecting Rainwater:
- Water should flow away from a building’s foundation.
- Water should not be directed onto neighboring properties or the sidewalk.
- Water can be captured in rain barrel for reuse, to water plants or wash cars.
- Downspouts can be extended to direct water under a deck, patio, or to a grassed or garden area.
- Rain gardens can be created and hard surfaces, like cement or patios, can be removed to allow water to infiltrate.

title: Income Savings Plan (ISP)
body:
The DHS Income Savings Plan (ISP) Program was created to help homeless clients build savings, transition out of shelters, and achieve self-sufficiency. Individuals who lived in a Department of Homeless Services shelter may have been required to participate in this program.
This program has ended.
Where you submit the request to reclaim the funds depends on how the funds were deposited.

title: Income Savings Plan (ISP)
section: Reclaim Funds Deposited to a Shelter ISP
body:
If you deposited funds directly with a shelter through their ISP, please contact that shelter directly to reclaim the funds.
If you don’t remember the name or address of the shelter, you can request this information by email or by phone.
By Email
Send an email to [RecordsAccess@dhs.nyc.gov](mailto:RecordsAccess@dhs.nyc.gov). Attach a completed DHS Record Release Authorization Form to your email. If you need to submit other supporting documents, include them in your email.
[Learn more and download the DHS Record Release Authorization Form on the DHS website.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/dhs/about/contact.page#:~:text=Requests%20for%20Client%20Records)
By Phone
- Agency: Department of Homeless Services
- Division: Office of the Ombudsman
- Phone Number: (800) 994-6494
- Business Hours: Monday - Friday: 9 AM - 5 PM
- Staff is available through the automated phone system during business hours.

links.text: Learn more and download the DHS Record Release Authorization Form on the DHS website.

title: Income Savings Plan (ISP)
section: Reclaim Funds Deposited to a DHS ISP
body:
If you deposited the funds by mailing a check or money order to a DHS/DSS ISP, savings that were not claimed by program participants were transferred to the NYS Office of Unclaimed Funds.
If you meet the following criteria, you can submit a claim to request your savings:
- You were enrolled in the program
- You have exited the shelter
- Have not yet claimed your savings
- Did not receive a refund from DHS
[Learn more on the NYS Office of Unclaimed Funds website.](https://www.osc.ny.gov/unclaimed-funds)

title: Warming Centers
body:
Call 911
Call 911   to report a medical or health-related emergency, or a person in need of medical assistance.
During periods of extreme cold, warming centers may be activated across all boroughs, using both fixed sites and warming vehicles.
When the Department of Social Services (DSS)/Department of Homeless Services (DHS) activate [Code Blue](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01037), resources and outreach are available. When a Code Blue is in effect, over 50 NYC hospitals (including [public hospitals](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02793)), as well as DHS [drop-in centers](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02528) and [shelters](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02501), operate with a full open-door policy. This ensures every New Yorker has a safe, warm place to go.
New Yorkers who see individuals they believe to be experiencing homelessness and in need should request [homeless outreach assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01037).

title: Pharmacy Home Delivery Program
body:
Gotham Health patients can get prescriptions delivered directly to their home through the Pharmacy Home Delivery Program.
To be eligible, you must have an active prescription from a Gotham Health provider.
Patients will receive their medications within one business day, with helpful tracking details via text, and they will be required to sign for their medications upon arrival. The program delivers all prescription medications except for controlled substances and refrigerated medications.
Patients can contact their health care provider to learn more.
- Agency: NYC Health + Hospitals
- Phone Number: (844) NYC-4NYC (844-692-4692)
- Business Hours: 24 hours, 7 days a week

title: NYC Affordability Resources
body:
Life in New York City is full of possibilities, but everyday costs can add up quickly.
This page brings together housing, food, health, transportation, and child care resources to help you lower your bills, meet essential needs, and make life more affordable.
Other ways to get help
- Screen for over 30 programs on [ACCESS NYC](https://access.nyc.gov/eligibility/) to check which benefits you may be eligible for.
- [Reach out](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/about-nyc-311/#contact-us) if you can’t find what you need or have questions about a program—we’re here to help!

title: NYC Affordability Resources
body:
+ − Find an affordable place to live Finding housing that fits your budget can be challenging. Housing is generally defined as affordable if it costs one-third or less of your income.
If you pay more, you’re not alone. Here’s where to look for affordable units with rents and maintenance costs that stay stable over time.
[Housing lotteries Enter lotteries to rent or buy below market rate apartments. ›](https://housingconnect.nyc.gov/PublicWeb/) [Public housing Apply for a NYCHA apartment with rent based on your income. ›](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01963) [Middle income housing developments Join waiting lists or enter lotteries for affordable rentals or co-ops. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/mitchell-lama-program.page) [Help buying your first home Receive up to $100,000 toward a down payment or closing costs of a new home. ›](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hpd/services-and-information/homefirst-down-payment-assistance-program.page)
+ − Pay rent and housing expenses Rising rents and housing costs can make it hard to keep up with bills.
You may qualify for programs that help pay rent, utilities, and other housing expenses.

+ − Keep your housing Facing the loss of your home can be stressful, but you don’t have to navigate this alone.
If you are at risk of eviction or foreclosure, there are programs and legal protections that may help you stay in your home and find a path forward.
Facing an immediate housing crisis?
- If you’re being evicted, contact [Homebase](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01041) for alternatives to shelter.
- If your home is unsafe due to domestic violence, contact [Safe Horizon](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01217) for emergency housing.

title: Street Health Outreach and Wellness (SHOW)
body:
Street Health Outreach and Wellness (SHOW) is a street medicine program that brings medical care, behavioral health resources, harm reduction, and material goods to New Yorkers who are homeless through mobile units.
Services include:
- Basic evaluation of symptoms or health concerns and treatment including wound care
- Screening, brief intervention, and referral to treatment for substance use disorders, including connection to medication-assisted treatment and additional support
- Overdose training and Narcan kit distribution
- Hygiene kits, reusable bags, snacks, and water
[Learn more about SHOW hours and locations.](https://www.nychealthandhospitals.org/street-health-outreach-wellness-mobile-units/#locations)

title: Elevate You Youth Behavioral Health Clinics
body:
New Yorkers ages 16 to 25 can access low-cost health services at Elevate You clinics. These clinics are for youth experiencing a mental health or substance use issue.
NYC Health + Hospitals and MetroPlusHealth established two youth clinics at NYC Health + Hospitals/Woodhull and Queens to help young New Yorkers access continuous and comprehensive care.
Elevate You clinics provide:
- Behavioral health care including medication management, individual and group therapy
- Life skills and pro-social development
- Vocational and academic support
- Social services support
- Connections to primary care and reproductive care
The program’s multidisciplinary treatment team includes a social worker, psychiatrist, nurse, youth peer, and family advocate.

title: Snow or Ice on Building
body:
Call 911
Call 911   to report immediate danger including:
- Falling ice or snow that is an immediate hazard
- An accident that just occurred and caused injury
New York City property owners and construction site managers are responsible for securing their properties from hazardous conditions, including melting or falling ice and snow.
The Department of Buildings (DOB) will take enforcement action if a building or site is not safely secured.
Residential and Commercial Buildings
Property owners should take all precautionary measures including, but not limited to:
- Securing and clearing roofs, awnings, umbrellas and overhangs of melting snow and ice.
- Removing ice and snow from tree limbs and other structures.
- Ensuring gutters are clear of debris to allow drainage.
Construction Sites
Builders, contractors, and developers should take all precautionary measures to secure construction sites, including but not limited to:
- Clearing icicles and snow masses from sidewalk sheds and supported and suspended scaffolds.
- Clearing melting snow and ice from roofs, overhangs, and gutters.
- Clearing debris from gutters and spouts to allow proper drainage.
- Clearing snow and ice from sidewalks, walkways and public areas surrounding a construction site.
- Call 911 if there is an emergency on a construction site.
You can report snow or ice on a building or construction site.
Include in your report:
- What is falling
- Which side of the building it's falling from
- What part of the structure it's falling from
File a Complaint
Snow or ice on a building reporting has ended for this year.

body:
The City announced the launch of the 2-K program, which will provide free child care for two-year-olds in New York City in Fall 2026.

- School Districts 18 and 23:  Canarsie, Rugby-Remsen Village, Brownsville and Ocean Hill as well as parts of East Flatbush- Farragut and Prospect Lefferts Garden-Wingate

title: Open Grid Security Gates
body:
New York City street-level stores and businesses must comply with new storefront security grille (gate) regulations outlined in the City's code. A storefront security-grille or security gate allows for:
- 24-hour visibility into a store or business
- Greater visual access for security
- Brighter, safer, and more welcoming NYC
By July 1, 2026 , all existing and new security gates in the City in buildings must comply with the [NYC Local Law 75 of 2009](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/local_laws/ll75of2009.pdf) requirement where 70 percent of the area covered by the security gate must be visible from the sidewalk.
This applies to buildings with occupancies designated as:
- Occupancy Group B (Business)
- Occupancy Group M (Mercantile)
Buildings in Historic districts and those designated as Landmark are exempt.
Business owners can get more information from the Department of Buildings.
[Learn more about open grid security gate requirements.](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/construction_advisories/sec_reqs.pdf)

title: SNAP Benefit Management
body:
You access SNAP benefits through an Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card.
Activating Your EBT Card
You need to activate the card before using it. Learn how to activate and manage your card on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page.
Where to Shop
You can use your EBT card to buy food at participating stores and farmers markets.
Some online stores also accept SNAP for delivery orders. Benefits may be used to pay for approved items, but not for delivery fees.
[Find stores, markets, and websites that accept SNAP.](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/retailer-locator)
What You Can Buy
You can use SNAP benefits to buy most food items.
You can’t use SNAP to buy:
- Alcoholic beverages or tobacco products
- Pet supplies
- Cleaning products, paper products, toiletries, or cooking utensils
- Items for food preservation, freezer containers, or food wrapping paper
- Medicine, vitamins, or minerals
[Learn more about eligible purchases.](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/eligible-food-items)
How to Pay
Once you’ve activated your new EBT card, you can use it to buy groceries. This works like a debit card. Just swipe the card and then enter your PIN in the machine at the checkout line.
After making your purchase, you should put a freeze on your card. Freezing your card when you’re not using it can help protect you from electronic benefit fraud. Learn more on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page.

body:
EBT scams are common. Some people will try to steal your benefits or trick you into giving your personal information. Personal information includes your Social Security number, bank information, EBT card number, or PIN number.
Follow these tips to keep your card secure.
- Freeze your card when you’re not using it with ebtEDGE. Only unfreeze it right before you buy something. [Learn how to freeze your card](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340).
- Check card readers for credit card skimmers.
- Keep your PIN safe. Only you should enter it.
- Always check and keep your receipts.

title: SNAP Benefit Management
body:
To receive SNAP, you might need to work, volunteer, do job training, or participate in other activities.
There are two types of work requirements:
- General requirements apply if you’re age 16 to 59 and able to work.
- ABAWD requirements may also apply if you’re age 18 to 64 and don’t have dependents.
General Work Requirements
Most people ages 16 to 59 must meet general work requirements to keep their benefits.
You may be exempt if you're doing one of the following:
- Working at least 30 hours per week or earning at least $217.50 per week
- Studying at least half-time
- Getting unemployment benefits
- Participating in addiction treatment
- Meeting TANF (Cash Assistance) work requirements
- Getting SSI (Supplemental Security Income)
[Learn more about general work requirements for SNAP.](https://otda.ny.gov/programs/snap/work-requirements.asp)
Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWD) Requirements
As of March 1, 2026, some SNAP recipients must comply with new ABAWD work requirements to keep their benefits.
Generally, you’re considered an ABAWD if you:
- Are age 18 through 64, and
- Don’t live with a child under 14, and
- Don’t have a physical or mental barrier that prevents you from working
HRA will inform you if you or anyone in your household needs to meet SNAP work requirements.
You can submit proof that you meet the SNAP work requirements on the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/).
[Learn more about ABAWD work rules.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/able-bodied-adults-without-dependents.page)

title: Electronic Benefit Theft and Scams
body: Some people will try to steal your SNAP and Cash Assistance benefits or scam you into giving your account and personal information. They use tactics like pretending to be from a government agency or tampering with devices to copy your EBT card details. This is called electronic benefit theft or fraud.

title: Electronic Benefit Theft and Scams
section: Types of Electronic Theft or Scams
body:
Skimming  is when someone puts an overlay on a store’s card-swiping machine to copy EBT, credit, and debit card account information. The stolen information is used to make fake cards called “clones.” The scammers will then steal money from the accounts.
Skimming can happen anywhere you swipe your EBT card. Your benefits can be stolen through skimming even if you always have possession of your EBT card.
Imposter scams  happen when thieves pretend to be from a government agency, such as the Department of Social Services (DSS) or the Human Resources Administration (HRA). This is sometimes called “third-party misrepresentation.” A caller or recorded message will ask for your account information, such as an EBT number or PIN. They may say you’re at risk of losing your benefits if you don’t. If you don’t currently receive SNAP, you might also get contacted by imposters that say you were chosen to receive SNAP.
Spoofing  refers to the tactic of falsifying data to gain access to your personal information. Scammers may forge their caller ID or email in order to impersonate DSS or HRA. Never give out personal information over the phone. Hang up and contact the organization through a verified number.
Phishing  is when thieves trick people into clicking on a link that allows them to access your account information. This usually happens through text or email.
[Learn more about EBT scams.](https://otda.ny.gov/workingfamilies/EBT-scam-alert.asp)

title: Electronic Benefit Theft and Scams
body:
- Freeze your card using [ebtEDGE](https://login5.fisglobal.com/idp/EBTEdge_NCH/?client_id) when you’re not using it. Only unfreeze it right before you buy something. Learn more on the [EBT Card Assistance](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02340) page.
- Check store machines for credit card skimmers before you use them.

title: SNAP Recertification
body:
To keep getting SNAP benefits, you must recertify to confirm you’re still eligible. Usually, you must recertify once a year. You’ll receive a notice in the mail or an alert on ACCESS HRA when it’s time to recertify.
It’s important to recertify as early as possible so you don’t miss a SNAP payment. You can recertify as early as 60 days before the end of your current recertification period.
[Recertify for SNAP on ACCESS HRA.](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/)
Already get SNAP?
- [Manage your benefits](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03714)
Steps to Recertify
- Fill out a recertification form . Answer questions about your household, income, and expenses. The fastest, easiest way is on the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/).
- Complete an interview by phone or in person. No appointment is needed. A SNAP eligibility worker will review your form with you to ensure that it’s ready for processing. They will also help you figure out which documents you need to provide.
- Submit required documents . You’ll find out during your interview which ones you need.
- Wait for a decision . This can take up to 30 days. You can check status on [ACCESS HRA](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/).

title: SNAP Recertification
body:
After your interview is finished and you’ve submitted your documents, HRA will start to process your recertification. It can take up to 30 days for HRA to review it and make a decision.
Getting a Decision
If your recertification is approved, HRA will mail you a letter to tell you. If you signed up for notifications, you will also get an email and text message.
If your recertification is rejected , HRA will mail you a letter to tell you why. You can reapply at any time. If your recertification wasn’t approved because you’re ineligible and your situation hasn’t changed, look into [other food help programs](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03304).
If you think HRA’s decision was wrong, you can:
- Visit a [SNAP center](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/locations/snap-locations.page) and request an informal conference
- Request a [Fair Hearing](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-02943)
Check Status
You can track your recertification and get notifications through the [ACCESS HRA website](https://a069-access.nyc.gov/accesshra/#/) or the [ACCESS HRA mobile app](https://www.nyc.gov/site/hra/help/accesshramobile.page).
If you can’t use ACCESS HRA, you can call for status.
Please note:
- Processing only starts after you finish your interview and send all documents.
- It can take up to 30 days to process your case.
If it’s been less than 30 days since you recertified, HRA’s phone line won’t have more information than you see on ACCESS HRA.

title: Cargo Drone Complaint
body:
Call 911
Call 911   to report a drone that is an immediate threat, safety risk, or interference with aircraft.
Need something else?
- [Drones](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-01541)
The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey (PANYNJ), in collaboration with New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC), are piloting a cargo drone program. The drone will be operated by Skyport Drone Services.
Cargo drones will transport non-hazardous, non-sensitive, and non-biological cargo between the Downtown Skyport (Pier 6) in Manhattan and the Brooklyn Marine Terminal (Pier 7). The focus of the pilot is to test whether drones can be used to deliver goods in the future. The goal is to reduce traffic, lower pollution, and find better ways to transport items instead of using trucks for mid-distance deliveries.
The pilot program will run on weekdays from 9 AM to 5 PM through April 2027.
You can file a complaint about:
- Drone activity near Pier 6 or Pier 7
- Activity within pilot zone areas
- General feedback and questions
Email [drones@panynj.gov](mailto:drones@panynj.gov) to report the problem.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026
body:
The City of New York, in partnership with the NYNJ Host Committee, has secured 1,000 affordable tickets to the FIFA World Cup 2026 for New Yorkers.
The tickets are $50 per seat and include free round-trip bus transportation to MetLife Stadium. The program covers the five group stage matches and two knockout round matches. Approximately 150 tickets will be allocated per game.
All current New York City residents over 15 years of age may enter the lottery for the chance to purchase tickets. Winners will be selected randomly.
Entry opens at [www.regnyctix.com](https://www.regnyctix.com) on Monday, May 25 at 10 AM and closes Saturday, May 30 at midnight. New Yorkers may enter once per day, with a daily cap of 50,000 entries.
Winners will be notified Wednesday, June 3, and may purchase up to two tickets each.
To prevent scalping, tickets will be nontransferable and distributed directly to winners at the official boarding location on the day of each match. Free round-trip transportation from the pickup location to the NYNJ Stadium will be included for every winner.

title: Hantavirus Information
body:
Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome is a rare but potentially serious disease. People exposed to rodents-infested environments are at the greatest risk for infections.
The best way to prevent hantavirus is to [control rodents both inside and outside the home](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/rats.page). You should take precautions when exposed to rodent infested environments.
There are no reported cases of Hantavirus in NYC.
[Learn more about the Hantavirus, including prevention and symptoms.](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/hantavirus-infection.page)

title: 2026 Primary Election
body:
In New York City, registered voters have three ways to cast their ballot.
1. Vote at a Poll Site
- During Early Voting (June 13 to June 21)
- On Election Day (June 23)
You must vote at the specific poll site assigned to our home address. Your Early Voting poll site may be different than your Election Day poll site.
[Learn more about voting at poll sites.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03691)
2. Vote by Early Mail Ballot
You can request an early mail ballot for any reason. The Board of Elections (BOE) will mail you the ballot and a pre-paid envelope. Then you can return the ballot by mail or drop it off at a poll site during voting hours or at a BOE office.
[Learn more and request an early mail ballot.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03687)
3. Vote by Absentee Ballot
If you can’t make it to the polls in person for a specific reason, like illness or travel, you can request an absentee ballot. The Board of Elections (BOE) will mail you the ballot and a pre-paid envelope. Then you can return the ballot by mail or drop it off at a poll site during voting hours or at a BOE office.
[Learn more and request an absentee ballot.](https://portal.311.nyc.gov/article/?kanumber=KA-03688)
